# Your CV stays in your repository.

::: {.lead}
Keep career evidence, reviewed Quarto documents and your agent instructions
together in a private workspace. Use cv-buid to connect that workspace to its
existing renderer, with deliberate edits and reviewable changes.
:::

[Connect an existing project](quick-start.qmd){.action-link}
:::

::: {.callout-note title="What works today"}
Adopt a project that already has a reviewed Python renderer. The toolkit adds a
small config and a project skill, then delegates build and watch commands to
that renderer. A bundled starter renderer remains on the [v1 checklist](v1.qmd).
:::

## A clear home for each source

::: {.ownership}
**Private profile** — career facts, evidence and review status.

**Reviewed QMD** — each résumé or CV's wording, selection and order.

**Presentation files** — Quarto settings, PDF styling and the optional Word reference.

**Project instructions** — your preferences and authority over the agent workflow.
:::

## Small commands, familiar rendering

After installation and adoption, from your private project:

```sh
cv-buid build
cv-buid build --watch
```

The reviewed renderer owns its output paths, fonts, locking and recovery behavior.
Your existing direct rendering command remains available. QMD is never regenerated
from historical JSON selections during a build.

## Review before sharing

Agents can inspect sources, propose evidence updates and show diffs. The owner
resolves uncertainty and approves factual changes. PDF and optional Word derive
from the same QMD, with separate presentation files and potentially different
pagination. Public exports use explicit field allowlists and remain staging files.

The adapter has passed package and macOS renderer acceptance checks. Native
Windows unit checks and complete renderer acceptance are distinct milestones;
see the [current verification boundary](v1.qmd#verification).
